MAGIC SEAS (Liberia-flagged bulker, IMO 9736169): Houthis claimed they attacked and sank the Magic Seas in the Red Sea with USVs, missiles and drones.
sources: https://www.ukmto.org/-/media/ukmto/products/20250711_ukmto_summary_report-11july25.pdf (UKMTO summary 11 Jul 2025, citing Reuters 07 Jul 2025 'Houthis claim first ship sinking this year')
note: Event 2025-07-06. UKMTO: attacked by up to 8 small craft/USVs, struck by missiles, crew abandoned ship, vessel reported sunk.

what: ETERNITY C (Liberia-flagged cargo ship, IMO 9588249): Houthi spokesman Saree claimed an unmanned boat and six cruise/ballistic missiles sank the Eternity C.
note: Event 2025-07-07/08. UKMTO: continuous small-craft and RPG attack, lost propulsion, sank. Claimed weapon mix (6 missiles) not detailed by UKMTO, which reports small craft and RPGs; sinking matches.

what: SCARLET RAY (Israeli-owned tanker/bulker, IMO 9799654): Houthis claimed a direct ballistic-missile hit on the Scarlet Ray near Yanbu.
sources: https://www.seatrade-maritime.com/security/houthi-claim-attack-on-msc-aby (Seatrade, 2025-09-02: 'claimed to have made a direct hit')
note: Event 2025-08-31. Attack happened, but UKMTO: splash ~20 m from the vessel, loud bang, no damage, crew safe, voyage continued. Claimed 'direct hit' contradicted; attempted attack confirmed.

what: MSC ABY (Liberia-flagged container ship): Houthis claimed a successful strike on MSC Aby in the northern Red Sea with two drones and a winged missile.
MINERVAGRACHT (Dutch-flagged cargo ship, Spliethoff): Saree claimed a cruise-missile strike on Minervagracht in the Gulf of Aden.
note: Event 2025-09-29, ~128 NM SE of Aden. UKMTO: hit by unknown projectile, fire, 2 injured, crew evacuated. Owner Spliethoff confirmed. MARAD later reports one mariner killed.

what: ENCELIA (Saudi-flagged tanker): Houthis claimed ballistic/cruise missiles and drones hit Encelia in the Red Sea, causing a large fire.
note: Event 2026-07-22 ~2000 UTC, 70 NM SW of Al Shuqaiq. UKMTO: tanker struck by unknown projectile, fire, no casualties. SPA confirmed fire at bow. UKMTO does not name the ship; SPA does.

what: LAYLA (Saudi-flagged / Bahri VLCC): Houthis claimed the same 22 July operation also hit Layla, causing a large fire.
NCC GHAZAL (Saudi-flagged product tanker, Bahri, IMO 9685205): Houthis claimed they fired ballistic missiles at NCC Ghazal in the Red Sea and forced it to turn back.
NCC WAFA (Saudi-flagged MR product tanker, Bahri, IMO 9688348): Saree claimed several ballistic missiles 'successfully targeted' Wafa in the northern Red Sea off Yanbu (the 'eighth' Saudi tanker).
DAISY (Dominica-flagged oil tanker, Bihar International): Saree claimed a ballistic missile 'successfully targeted' the Saudi tanker Daisy in the Gulf of Aden.
outcome_sources: https://gcaptain.com/houthis-escalate-red-sea-campaign-claim-eighth-saudi-tanker-attack/ (gCaptain, 2026-08-05: UKMTO tanker ~95 NM SE of Aden, loud explosion close by)
note: Event 2026-08-05 ~1730 local. UKMTO/JMIC: master reported a loud explosion close by; the shockwave caused minor damage; crew safe; ship went on to Djibouti. A near miss with minor damage rather than a direct hit. Doubt: MARAD advisory 2026-013 says Daisy was struck off Yanbu on 24 Aug, which looks like a MARAD error.

what: TIHAMAH (Tanzania-flagged general cargo/deck cargo ship, Egyptian-owned): Houthis claimed they attacked a ship in Bab el-Mandeb carrying Saudi military equipment.
note: Event 2026-08-11 early morning, anchored ~5 NM off Al Mokha. UKMTO: general cargo vessel struck amidships by unknown projectile, fire. 4 crew and 2 coast guard rescuers killed (Yemeni sources). The strike is confirmed; the claimed military cargo is disputed (Yemeni Transport Ministry says food). JMIC still said 'not claimed' when it published, before the Houthi claim later that day. | JMIC 083 (11.08) says the group had not claimed it at report time; Saba claim same day (JPost/Reuters).

what: AMZAN (Saudi-flagged VLCC, Bahri): Houthis claimed a precise ballistic-missile hit on Amzan off Yanbu that set it on fire.
note: Event 2026-08-24 0637 UTC, 63 NM W of Yanbu. UKMTO: tanker struck by unknown projectile, fire on main deck, crew safe. Bahri confirmed an incident involving Amzan; Lloyd's List Intelligence Red Sea Brief 27 Aug confirms.
